title: Three.js Small Examples
description: Use these small Three.js examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Draw your first cube
examples.description: A mesh joins a shape with a material. The scene holds the mesh, and the renderer draws it from the camera's view.
examples.output: A blue cube appears on the new canvas, turned slightly so its shape is visible.

examples.title: Move the camera
examples.description: The camera is the viewpoint into a scene.
examples.output: The camera looks down at the cube from the side and above.

examples.title: Choose a different geometry
examples.description: Geometry describes an object's shape. A sphere geometry uses small triangles to approximate a round surface.
examples.output: A blue ball is drawn instead of the cube.

examples.title: Show the shape as lines
examples.description: A material tells the renderer how a shape should look.
examples.output: The cube appears as blue lines rather than filled faces.

examples.title: Place an object
examples.description: An object's position moves it along three scene axes: x, y and z.
examples.output: The cube moves right and upward relative to this camera view.

examples.title: Turn an object
examples.description: Rotation turns an object around an axis.
examples.output: The cube is turned 45 degrees around y and 22.5 degrees around x.

examples.title: Resize an object with scale
examples.description: Scale multiplies an object's size on each axis.
examples.output: The cube becomes twice as wide and half as tall, while its depth stays unchanged.

examples.title: Move a group together
examples.description: A Group can hold several objects. Moving the group moves all its children together.
examples.output: Two cubes appear together, positioned as one group.

examples.title: Light a shaded material
examples.description: Some materials respond to light. MeshStandardMaterial needs lighting so its surfaces can show shape and shading.
examples.output: The cube faces have different brightness because of the light direction.

examples.title: Animate using time
examples.description: An animation loop draws new frames. Using elapsed time makes motion less dependent on how many frames the device can draw.
examples.output: The cube turns continuously around its y axis.

examples.title: Resize the camera view
examples.description: A perspective camera needs the canvas aspect ratio.
examples.output: The canvas becomes wider while the camera uses the matching shape.

examples.title: Clean up a scene
examples.description: GPU resources need explicit cleanup when a scene is no longer used.
examples.output: Calling disposeScene removes this example's canvas and releases its owned resources.
